name: All Fours (Yorkshire)
description: West Yorkshire All Fours is a cherished pub league tradition in Northern England, particularly centered in the Heavy Woollen District (Batley, Heckmondwike). Unlike the classic game, it uses a 'Pitch' start with no turn-up card and features unique regional etiquette such as the 'First Trick Face Up' rule.

overview.description: West Yorkshire All Fours is a cherished pub league tradition in Northern England, particularly centered in the Heavy Woollen District (Batley, Heckmondwike). Unlike the classic game, it uses a 'Pitch' start with no turn-up card and features unique regional etiquette such as the 'First Trick Face Up' rule.

history.origins: Rooted in the industrial heartlands of Yorkshire, the game evolved alongside the textile mills. It became a formalized league sport in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 1800s: Traditional All Fours is adopted in Yorkshire taverns.
1950s: Formal leagues (like the Heckmondwike league) establish standardized regional rules.
2003: Documented extensively by card historians John and Anita Dunning.
history.cultural: Matches are traditionally held in 'Tap Rooms' of pubs. The game is known for its steady, methodical pace and strict observance of 'The Pitch'.
history.evolution: Yorkshire play stabilized around an 11-point target and the 'Low-to-Holder' rule, specifically rejecting the Lancashire 'Low-is-Taken' innovation.

setup.players: 4 players in two partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 6 cards in batches of 3. No card is turned for trump.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, All Fours pegging board (traditionally to 11 points).

rules.objective: First team to reach 11 points (or 15 in some leagues) by winning High, Low, Jack, and Game.
rules.gameplay: 1. The player to dealer's left pitches the first card; its suit becomes trump. 2. The first trick is kept face up with a trump visible on top; later tricks are face down. 3. If a player has no trumps and no counting cards above 9 and is not winning the current trick, they may throw in their hand and take no further part while partner continues. 4. Score points in order High, Low, Jack, Game.
keyRules: High (1 pt): Team dealt the highest trump.
Low (1 pt): Team dealt the lowest trump (unlike Lancashire, this is awarded to the holder).
Jack (1 pt): Winning the trick containing the Jack of trumps.
Game (1 pt): Higher pip total (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1, 10=10).
Pitcher's partner must keep their cards face down until the Pitch is made.

strategy.basic: If your hand is weak but contains a lone 10, try to play it on your partner's lead early to guarantee it isn't 'filtered' out by the opponents.
strategy.intermediate: The Throw-in: Use the 'no trumps, no count' rule strategically to reset a hand where the opponents likely have all the power cards.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Pitching: If you have a poor hand, pitch a suit where you hold a 'bobby' (low card) in hopes that your partner can dominate with the High or Jack.
tips: Count the pips constantly. Since A, K, Q, J, 10 represent all the value, knowing who has captured a 10 is the key to predicting the 'Game' point.
Remember that 'Low' is for the card dealt. Even if you lose your 2 of trumps on the first trick, your side still pegs the point at the end.

variations.name: Heckmondwike League Standard
variations.description: Played to 15 points instead of 11 to allow for longer, more strategic matches.

scoring.description: Classic All Fours scoring system focused on the four specific points.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 11 points wins. The strict H-L-J-G counting order is used to resolve 11-11 ties within a single hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: Step into the tap rooms of Batley and Heckmondwike with Yorkshire's pitch-led All Fours and precise H-L-J-G pegging.
